propositions: A failed tickets-branch push is unobservable on async, library, and MCP write paths: the rejection warning is discarded by OS stderr redirection, absent logging handler, or server-only stderr routing respectively.
The async path spawns a detached child with DEVNULL stderr and start_new_session=True without waiting, making every warning the child emits discarded by the OS.

Library embedders attach only a NullHandler to the rebar root; install_stderr_handler runs only from CLI and MCP server, so in-process rebar.comment() calls return normally with no push status signal.
The MCP tool targets the server's stderr but the agent reads only the tool result; comment_ticket against a declining remote returned {result: ok} with commits stranded locally.

A durable push_state marker in the git dir records failures at the single _raise_if_strict choke point, exposed via rebar.push_status() for library embedders and a push_status field on MCP write-tool outputs.
The marker clears on successful push, preserving the best-effort contract that push_tickets_branch always returns None and never raises.
